```{r}
#| include: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(comment = "", message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
options(width = 160)
```

This notebook reads the files in `example/` into R and checks every part of
the format against them. Its twin, `notebook-python.qmd`, does the same in
Python, section by section. `SPEC.md` states the rules and `RATIONALE.md` the
reasons; section numbers such as S4 or T3 refer to both. Every output below comes from running the code.

It belongs to the **package suite**: it builds the package's own objects from
the files, on an unreviewed branch build, to test that the files hold
everything an analysis needs. The checks of the format that need no package
are in `verify/`.

`example/` was written by R (`package-suite/make_example.R`) from sceptre's built-in data:

| Dataset | Cells | Responses | gRNAs | Analyses |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `highmoi` | 500 | 100 | 60 | `left_sided`, `two_sided`, `singleton`, `bonferroni`, `stopped_after_qc`, `with_resamples` |
| `lowmoi` | 1,000 | 100 | 50 | `default` |
| `types` | 6 | 3 | 2 | none: a synthetic data file with every kind of column |

The Python notebook runs first. It adds the analysis `continued_in_python` and
writes its own copy of everything to `roundtrip/python-copy`, which this
notebook reads.

```{r}
source("package-suite/setup.R")
screen <- "example/highmoi/screen.h5mu"
analyses <- "example/highmoi/analyses"
show_table <- function(...) print(data.frame(..., check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE, right = FALSE)
```

## 1. What is on disk

One file holds the data. Each analysis is a folder.

```{r}
file_listing(file.path(analyses, "left_sided"))
```

**The data file** is a MuData file. Its modalities are named for what was
measured: `rna` here, and `grna` for the gRNAs (S2). Counts are 32-bit integers,
cells × features, compressed by feature, with 64-bit column pointers (S3, S4).
The file's own metadata is a small native record, which carries the data
file's format version (S10).

```{r}
rhdf5::h5readAttributes(screen, "mod/rna/X")[c("encoding-type", "shape")]
count_types(screen)
str(rhdf5::h5read(screen, "uns/sceptre"))
```

**An analysis** starts by naming its data file and which modality of it is
the response (A1). It has a format version of its own:

```{r}
cat(readLines(file.path(analyses, "left_sided/analysis.json")), sep = "\n")
```

Each completed stage has a record, written after the stage's tables. It holds
the stage's settings and lists the files the stage wrote (A2):

```{r}
cat(readLines(file.path(analyses, "left_sided/calibration/record.json")), sep = "\n")
```

The tables, with their columns:

```{r}
saved <- fmt_read_analysis(file.path(analyses, "left_sided"))
for (table in names(saved$tables)) {
    columns <- vapply(saved$tables[[table]], function(x) class(x)[1], character(1))
    cat(sprintf("%-36s %5d rows: %s\n", table, nrow(saved$tables[[table]]), paste0(names(columns), " (", columns, ")", collapse = ", ")))
}
```

## 2. The data file as a SingleCellExperiment

`fmt_read_screen()` uses only Bioconductor's `MuData`; it needs no sceptre code.

```{r}
sce <- fmt_read_screen(screen)
sce
str(metadata(sce)$sceptre)
```

Cell covariates are split in the file (S5): facts about the cell in a shared
table, measurements of a modality in that modality's table. In R they arrive
as one table, a modality's columns prefixed with its name:

```{r}
head(as.data.frame(colData(sce)), 3)
```

The sceptre package calls the response modality `response` whatever was
measured, so in a `sceptre_object` these columns are `response_n_umis` and so
on, as they are today. `read_sceptre_object()` (section 3) does that renaming.

The gRNA counts are the alternative experiment `gRNA`; its `rowData` is the
gRNA table (S8). Its coordinate columns say what they locate: the target.

```{r}
as.data.frame(rowData(altExp(sce, "gRNA")))[c(1, 2, 11, 12, 59, 60), ]
```

## 3. An analysis as a `sceptre_object`

`read_sceptre_object()` builds sceptre's own object from the data file and one
analysis folder.

```{r}
object <- read_sceptre_object(screen, file.path(analyses, "left_sided"))
object
```

```{r}
head(as.data.frame(get_result(object, "run_discovery_analysis")), 6)
```

The object behaves as one that was never saved; its plots work:

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
plot(object)
```

## 4. Reading back what the files imply

Several things a package needs are not stored, because they follow from what
is (principle 7). This section rebuilds each one from the files with plain R
and compares it with an independent source: the `sceptre_object` the analysis
was written from, kept in `example-objects.rds` from the session that ran it.

```{r}
originals <- readRDS("package-suite/example-objects.rds")
original <- originals$highmoi$left_sided
tables <- saved$tables
records <- saved$stages
cells <- colnames(sce)
grna <- altExp(sce, "gRNA")
```

**Negative-control groups (T4).** The members of each control group are read
from a table, never taken apart from the group's name.

```{r}
groups <- tables[["calibration/negative_control_groups"]]
members <- split(groups$grna_id, groups$grna_group)
head(members, 4)
```

```{r}
non_targeting <- rownames(grna)[rowData(grna)$grna_target == "non-targeting"]
show_table(check = c(
    "control groups", "gRNAs per group", "every member is a non-targeting gRNA",
    "every group in the calibration results has members"
), value = vapply(list(
    length(members), paste(sort(unique(lengths(members))), collapse = ", "),
    all(groups$grna_id %in% non_targeting),
    setequal(tables[["calibration/results"]]$grna_target, names(members))
), as.character, character(1)))
```

**Per-target and per-control cell lists (T1).** The assignment table has one
row per (gRNA, cell). Pooling a target's gRNAs gives the cells a package tests.

```{r}
grna_table <- data.frame(grna_id = rownames(grna), as.data.frame(rowData(grna)))
grna_table$grna_group <- grna_groups(grna_table, records$parameters$settings$grna_integration_strategy)
by_grna <- cells_by_grna(tables[["assignment/assignments"]], rownames(grna), cells)
pooled <- group_cells(by_grna, grna_table)
show_table(check = c(
    "gRNAs", "targets", "non-targeting gRNAs", "per-gRNA lists identical to the object's",
    "per-target unions and per-control lists identical to the object's", "gRNAs per cell identical to the object's"
), value = vapply(list(
    length(by_grna), length(pooled$grna_group_idxs), length(pooled$indiv_nt_grna_idxs),
    identical(by_grna, field(original, "initial_grna_assignment_list")),
    identical(pooled, field(original, "grna_assignments_raw")),
    identical(grnas_per_cell(by_grna, length(cells)), field(original, "grnas_per_cell"))
), as.character, character(1)))
```

**Which results are significant (T5).** The table does not store the column.
The stage record stores one number, the largest p-value called significant.

```{r}
threshold <- records$discovery$significance_threshold
derived <- add_significant(tables[["discovery/results"]], threshold)
theirs <- as.data.frame(get_result(original, "run_discovery_analysis"))
both <- merge(derived, theirs, by = c("grna_target", "response_id"), suffixes = c("", "_original"))
show_table(check = c("threshold in the record", "called significant", "identical to the column R computed, for every pair"),
    value = c(format(threshold, digits = 17), sum(derived$significant, na.rm = TRUE), identical(both$significant, both$significant_original)))
```

**The log2 fold change (T5).** A results table that has `fold_change` does not
store `log_2_fold_change`; a reader computes it as `log(fold_change) / log(2)`,
which is sceptre's own formula. Under the bonferroni strategy sceptre reports
only the log2 value, so there it is the stored column.

```{r}
effect_columns <- function(table) paste(intersect(names(table), c("fold_change", "se_fold_change", "log_2_fold_change")), collapse = ", ")
discovery <- tables[["discovery/results"]]
both <- merge(add_log_2_fold_change(discovery), theirs, by = c("grna_target", "response_id"), suffixes = c("", "_original"))
bonferroni <- fmt_read_analysis(file.path(analyses, "bonferroni"))$tables[["discovery/results"]]
show_table(check = c("effect columns stored (union strategy)", "derived log2 identical to R's column, for every pair",
    "effect columns stored (bonferroni strategy)"),
    value = c(effect_columns(discovery), identical(both$log_2_fold_change, both$log_2_fold_change_original), effect_columns(bonferroni)))
```

**The design matrix (T7).** The record stores the formula and a hash. R
rebuilds the matrix with `model.matrix()` from the formula and the covariates
in the data file.

```{r}
settings <- records$parameters$settings
design <- model.matrix(as.formula(settings$formula), as.data.frame(colData(sce)))
show_table(check = c("formula", "terms rebuilt", "terms equal to the record's", "hash in the record", "hash of the matrix rebuilt here", "equal"),
    value = c(
        settings$formula, paste(colnames(design), collapse = ", "),
        identical(colnames(design), as.character(records$parameters$design$terms)),
        paste0(substr(records$parameters$design$sha256, 1, 16), "..."),
        paste0(substr(design_sha256(design), 1, 16), "..."),
        identical(design_sha256(design), records$parameters$design$sha256)
    ))
```

Only additive formulas of covariate names, `log(x)` and `log(x + 1)` can be
written:

```{r}
formulas <- c(settings$formula, "~log(rna_n_umis) * batch", "~poly(rna_n_umis, 2)")
show_table(can_be_written = vapply(formulas, formula_in_subset, logical(1)), formula = formulas)
```

**Resampled statistics (T5).** `with_resamples` kept every resampled statistic.
In the file they are one list per pair; sceptre gets them back as the columns
it expects.

```{r}
resamples <- fmt_read_analysis(file.path(analyses, "with_resamples"))$tables[["discovery/resamples"]]
wide <- as.data.frame(get_result(read_sceptre_object(screen, file.path(analyses, "with_resamples")), "run_discovery_analysis"))
show_table(check = c("pairs", "statistics per pair", "columns in the file's table", "z_null_ columns in the object's table"),
    value = c(nrow(resamples), paste(range(lengths(resamples$z_null)), collapse = " to "),
        paste(names(resamples), collapse = ", "), length(resample_columns(wide))))
```

## 5. Several analyses, two datasets

Each dataset is read from one file; only the analysis differs.

```{r}
analysis_folders <- function(dataset) list.dirs(file.path("example", dataset, "analyses"), recursive = FALSE)
do.call(rbind, lapply(c("highmoi", "lowmoi"), function(dataset) {
    do.call(rbind, lapply(analysis_folders(dataset), function(folder) {
        a <- fmt_read_analysis(folder)
        s <- a$stages
        discovery <- a$tables[["discovery/results"]]
        data.frame(
            dataset = dataset, analysis = basename(folder), stages_run = paste(names(s), collapse = ", "),
            side = s$parameters$settings$side, strategy = s$parameters$settings$grna_integration_strategy,
            control_group = s$parameters$settings$control_group, assignment = s$assignment$settings$method,
            cells_in_use = sum(a$tables[["qc/cells"]]$in_use),
            discoveries = if (is.null(discovery)) "" else as.character(sum(add_significant(discovery, s$discovery$significance_threshold)$significant, na.rm = TRUE))
        )
    }))
}))
```

## 6. Round trip in R

Each analysis is read from the files into a `sceptre_object` and compared,
field by field, with the object it was written from.

"Identical" is R's `identical()`. "Equal" is `all.equal()`: the same values in
another storage type. Tables are compared with their rows sorted, because the
files keep tables sorted by key and not in the order a session happened to
hold them (T0).

```{r}
compare_with_originals <- function(root) {
    do.call(rbind, lapply(names(originals), function(dataset) {
        do.call(rbind, lapply(names(originals[[dataset]]), function(name) {
            folder <- if (name == "imported") NULL else file.path(root, dataset, "analyses", name)
            back <- suppressMessages(read_sceptre_object(file.path(root, dataset, "screen.h5mu"), folder))
            verdict <- compare_objects(originals[[dataset]][[name]], back)
            data.frame(
                dataset = dataset, object = name, fields = length(verdict), identical = sum(verdict == "identical"),
                equal = sum(verdict == "equal"), different = sum(!verdict %in% c("identical", "equal")),
                equal_not_identical = paste(names(verdict)[verdict == "equal"], collapse = ", ")
            )
        }))
    }))
}
compare_with_originals("example")
```

The fields that are equal but not identical:

- `grna_target_data_frame`: the gRNA table's `start` column was an integer
  with missing values and is stored as doubles (S7).
- `grna_assignment_hyperparameters`: the threshold `5` was a double in R and
  comes back as an integer, because JSON does not tell the two apart.
- `discovery_pairs` (low MOI): a table class, not its contents.

Writing the objects just read to a new folder gives the same files:

```{r}
r_written <- lapply(originals, function(objects) setdiff(names(objects), "imported"))
copy <- "roundtrip/r-copy"
unlink(copy, recursive = TRUE)
for (dataset in names(r_written)) {
    source_screen <- file.path("example", dataset, "screen.h5mu")
    write_sceptre_screen(read_sceptre_object(source_screen), file.path(copy, dataset, "screen.h5mu"),
        response_names = rowData(fmt_read_screen(source_screen))$response_name)
    for (name in r_written[[dataset]]) {
        loaded <- suppressMessages(read_sceptre_object(source_screen, file.path("example", dataset, "analyses", name)))
        write_sceptre_analysis(loaded, file.path(copy, dataset, "screen.h5mu"), file.path(copy, dataset, "analyses", name))
    }
}
compare_files <- function(root) {
    do.call(rbind, lapply(names(r_written), function(dataset) {
        do.call(rbind, lapply(r_written[[dataset]], function(name) {
            a <- fmt_read_analysis(file.path("example", dataset, "analyses", name))
            b <- fmt_read_analysis(file.path(root, dataset, "analyses", name))
            data.frame(
                dataset = dataset, analysis = name,
                link_equal = isTRUE(all.equal(a$screen, b$screen)) && identical(a$response_modality, b$response_modality),
                stage_records_equal = isTRUE(all.equal(a$stages, b$stages)), tables = length(a$tables),
                tables_identical = sum(mapply(identical, a$tables, b$tables[names(a$tables)]))
            )
        }))
    }))
}
compare_files(copy)
```

## 7. Across languages

`roundtrip/python-copy` was written by the Python notebook: pysceptre read
every example and wrote it out again. R reads the Python-written files and
compares the objects with the originals.

```{r}
compare_with_originals("roundtrip/python-copy")
```

File by file, the Python-written copy holds what the R-written example holds:

```{r}
compare_files("roundtrip/python-copy")
```

The data files written by the two languages have the same number types and the
same contents:

```{r}
do.call(rbind, lapply(names(r_written), function(dataset) {
    a <- fmt_read_screen(file.path("example", dataset, "screen.h5mu"))
    b <- fmt_read_screen(file.path("roundtrip/python-copy", dataset, "screen.h5mu"))
    data.frame(
        dataset = dataset,
        count_types_equal = identical(count_types(file.path("example", dataset, "screen.h5mu")), count_types(file.path("roundtrip/python-copy", dataset, "screen.h5mu"))),
        counts_identical = identical(counts(a), counts(b)) && identical(counts(altExp(a, "gRNA")), counts(altExp(b, "gRNA"))),
        covariates_identical = identical(as.data.frame(colData(a)), as.data.frame(colData(b))),
        grna_table_identical = identical(as.data.frame(rowData(altExp(a, "gRNA"))), as.data.frame(rowData(altExp(b, "gRNA")))),
        metadata_identical = identical(metadata(a), metadata(b))
    )
}))
```

## 8. Continue an analysis across languages

This section is about parity between the two packages, not about the format:
the format's part is only to carry what each needs to continue.

**Python continued R's analysis.** `stopped_after_qc` was run in R through QC.
The Python notebook read it, ran the three testing stages in pysceptre and
saved `continued_in_python`. R reads that as a `sceptre_object`. Each stage
record says which package ran the stage:

```{r}
continued <- read_sceptre_object(screen, file.path(analyses, "continued_in_python"))
do.call(rbind, lapply(attr(continued, "format_provenance"), as.data.frame))
```

Its discovery p-values next to those R computed with the same settings
(`left_sided`):

```{r}
both <- merge(
    as.data.frame(get_result(continued, "run_discovery_analysis")),
    as.data.frame(get_result(original, "run_discovery_analysis")),
    by = c("response_id", "grna_target"), suffixes = c("_python", "_r")
)
tested <- both$pass_qc_python & both$pass_qc_r
show_table(check = c("pairs", "tested in both", "largest relative difference in p-value", "discoveries, Python", "discoveries, R"),
    value = c(nrow(both), sum(tested), format(max(abs(both$p_value_python[tested] / both$p_value_r[tested] - 1)), digits = 2),
        sum(both$significant_python, na.rm = TRUE), sum(both$significant_r, na.rm = TRUE)))
```

**R continues from Python-written files.** R reads `stopped_after_qc` from the
copy that Python wrote, runs the remaining stages, and compares with the
analysis that R ran without ever saving.

```{r}
resumed <- read_sceptre_object("roundtrip/python-copy/highmoi/screen.h5mu", "roundtrip/python-copy/highmoi/analyses/stopped_after_qc") |>
    run_calibration_check(parallel = FALSE, print_progress = FALSE) |>
    run_power_check(parallel = FALSE, print_progress = FALSE) |>
    run_discovery_analysis(parallel = FALSE, print_progress = FALSE)
results_identical <- vapply(c("run_calibration_check", "run_power_check", "run_discovery_analysis"), function(stage) {
    identical(rows_sorted(get_result(resumed, stage)), rows_sorted(get_result(original, stage)))
}, logical(1))
show_table(result = names(results_identical), identical_to_the_never_saved_analysis = results_identical)
```

## 9. What a reader tolerates and what it refuses

```{r}
variants <- "roundtrip/variants-r"
unlink(variants, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(variants, recursive = TRUE)
variant <- function(name) {
    # a fresh copy of the left_sided analysis to modify
    file.copy(file.path(analyses, "left_sided"), variants, recursive = TRUE)
    file.rename(file.path(variants, "left_sided"), file.path(variants, name))
    file.path(variants, name)
}
attempt <- function(read) {
    tryCatch({
        read
        cat("Read without complaint.\n")
    }, error = function(e) cat("Refused:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"))
}
```

**A table in pieces, with an unknown column and dictionary-encoded identifiers
(T0).** The assignment table is replaced by a folder of three part files.

```{r}
folder <- variant("parts")
table <- nanoparquet::read_parquet(file.path(folder, "assignment/assignments.parquet"))
unlink(file.path(folder, "assignment/assignments.parquet"))
dir.create(file.path(folder, "assignment/assignments.parquet"))
pieces <- split(seq_len(nrow(table)), cut(seq_len(nrow(table)), 3, labels = FALSE))
for (i in seq_along(pieces)) {
    part <- data.frame(
        grna_id = factor(table$grna_id[pieces[[i]]]),   # a factor is written dictionary-encoded
        cell_id = factor(table$cell_id[pieces[[i]]]),
        score = seq(0, 1, length.out = length(pieces[[i]]))   # a column this reader does not know
    )
    nanoparquet::write_parquet(part, file.path(folder, "assignment/assignments.parquet", sprintf("part-%05d.parquet", i - 1L)))
}
list.files(file.path(folder, "assignment/assignments.parquet"))
comparison_summary(compare_objects(original, read_sceptre_object(screen, folder)))
```

The same variant written by Python (three part files from `pyarrow`) reads the
same way:

```{r}
comparison_summary(compare_objects(original, read_sceptre_object(screen, "roundtrip/variants-python/parts")))
```

**Another data file (A1).** An analysis refuses a data file that was subset,
even if it kept the dataset's identifier, and a data file that was imported
again.

```{r}
subset <- sce[, 1:400]
fmt_write_screen(subset, file.path(variants, "subset.h5mu"))
attempt(read_sceptre_object(file.path(variants, "subset.h5mu"), file.path(analyses, "left_sided")))

again <- sce
metadata(again)$sceptre$id <- NULL                     # no identifier: the writer assigns a new one
fmt_write_screen(again, file.path(variants, "imported_again.h5mu"))
attempt(read_sceptre_object(file.path(variants, "imported_again.h5mu"), file.path(analyses, "left_sided")))
```

**Modality names, and modalities an analysis does not use (S2, A1).** The same
data is written under the modality name `atac`, with a hashing modality beside
it. With two candidates, a reader must be told which is the response; an
analysis folder says so itself.

```{r}
other <- object_screen(originals$highmoi$imported, id = metadata(sce)$sceptre$id, response_modality = "atac")
hto <- Matrix::sparseMatrix(i = rep(1:2, length.out = ncol(other)), j = seq_len(ncol(other)), x = 5,
    dims = c(2, ncol(other)), dimnames = list(c("hto_1", "hto_2"), colnames(other)))
altExp(other, "hashing") <- SingleCellExperiment(assays = list(counts = hto))
fmt_write_screen(other, file.path(variants, "atac_with_hashing.h5mu"))
names(count_types(file.path(variants, "atac_with_hashing.h5mu")))
attempt(fmt_read_screen(file.path(variants, "atac_with_hashing.h5mu")))
```

```{r}
check_other <- function(file, folder) {
    back <- read_sceptre_object(file, folder)
    show_table(check = c("response modality named by the analysis", "formula in the parameters record", "object compared with the original"),
        value = c(fmt_response_modality(folder), read_json(file.path(folder, "parameters/record.json"))$settings$formula,
            comparison_summary(compare_objects(original, back))))
}
write_sceptre_analysis(original, file.path(variants, "atac_with_hashing.h5mu"), file.path(variants, "atac_analysis"), response_modality = "atac")
check_other(file.path(variants, "atac_with_hashing.h5mu"), file.path(variants, "atac_analysis"))
```

The same variant written by Python reads the same way:

```{r}
check_other("roundtrip/variants-python/atac_with_hashing.h5mu", "roundtrip/variants-python/atac_analysis")
```

**A table that is not what its stage wrote (A5).** Each stage record lists its
files and their row counts.

```{r}
folder <- variant("truncated")
cells_table <- nanoparquet::read_parquet(file.path(folder, "qc/cells.parquet"))
nanoparquet::write_parquet(cells_table[1:450, ], file.path(folder, "qc/cells.parquet"))
attempt(fmt_read_analysis(folder))
```

**Rerunning a stage (A4).** Clearing a stage removes its record and files and
those of every later stage, so the folder never holds stale results.

```{r}
folder <- variant("rerun")
cat("before:", fmt_stages_run(folder), "-", length(list.files(folder, recursive = TRUE)), "files\n")
fmt_clear_stage(folder, "qc")
cat("after: ", fmt_stages_run(folder), "-", length(list.files(folder, recursive = TRUE)), "files\n")
cat("last step of the object read from it:", sceptre:::last_function_called(read_sceptre_object(screen, folder)), "\n")
```

**The fit cache (T6).** Fitted response models are kept in `fits/response/`,
outside the stage folders: no stage owns them, and any testing stage can use
or add to them. Clearing a testing stage leaves them; clearing QC removes them.

```{r}
folder <- variant("fits_kept")
fmt_clear_stage(folder, "calibration")
cat("after clearing calibration:", fmt_stages_run(folder), "- fits kept:", file.exists(file.path(folder, "fits/response/identity.json")), "\n")
fmt_clear_stage(folder, "qc")
cat("after clearing qc:         ", fmt_stages_run(folder), "- fits kept:", file.exists(file.path(folder, "fits/response/identity.json")), "\n")
```

A cached fit is reused only if it was made as this analysis would make it.
Here the record of how the fits were made is changed to another fitting
method.

```{r}
cat("fits reused as written:", length(sceptre:::response_fits(object)), "\n")
folder <- variant("other_fit_method")
identity <- read_json(file.path(folder, "fits/response/identity.json"))
identity$response_fit_method <- "sceptre"
write_json(identity, file.path(folder, "fits/response/identity.json"))
changed <- read_sceptre_object(screen, folder)
cat("fits reused after the change:", length(sceptre:::response_fits(changed)), "\n")
```

**Every kind of column (S7).** `example/types/screen.h5mu` is a small synthetic
data file written by R with a factor whose levels are not alphabetical, a text
covariate, a true/false covariate, a covariate with missing values, and a gRNA
table with missing text and a missing integer. R reads it back:

```{r}
describe <- function(frame) {
    frame <- as.data.frame(frame)
    kind <- vapply(frame, function(column) {
        if (is.factor(column)) return(paste0("categorical: ", paste(levels(column), collapse = ", ")))
        if (is.integer(column)) "integer" else if (is.double(column)) "double" else "text"
    }, character(1))
    values <- vapply(frame, function(column) {
        text <- if (is.double(column)) format(column, drop0trailing = TRUE, trim = TRUE) else as.character(column)
        paste(ifelse(is.na(column), "NA", text), collapse = ", ")
    }, character(1))
    data.frame(column = names(frame), kind = unname(kind), values = unname(values))
}
from_r <- fmt_read_screen("example/types/screen.h5mu")
print(rbind(describe(colData(from_r)), describe(rowData(altExp(from_r, "gRNA")))), row.names = FALSE, right = FALSE)
```

Text and true/false covariates have become categoricals, and the integer
column with a missing value has become doubles, as S7 says. The Python
notebook built the same data itself and wrote it; R reads that file to the
same result:

```{r}
from_python <- fmt_read_screen("roundtrip/python-copy/types/screen.h5mu")
show_table(check = c("covariates identical to the R-written file's", "gRNA table identical", "counts identical", "count types equal"),
    value = c(
        identical(describe(colData(from_python)), describe(colData(from_r))),
        identical(describe(rowData(altExp(from_python, "gRNA"))), describe(rowData(altExp(from_r, "gRNA")))),
        identical(counts(from_python), counts(from_r)) && identical(counts(altExp(from_python, "gRNA")), counts(altExp(from_r, "gRNA"))),
        identical(count_types("roundtrip/python-copy/types/screen.h5mu"), count_types("example/types/screen.h5mu"))
    ))
```

**A covariate with a dot in its name (S5.4, T7.1).** The types file has the
covariate `S.Score`. R builds the design matrix for a formula that uses it and
compares it with the one the Python notebook built for the same formula.

```{r}
dotted <- model.matrix(~ log(rna_n_umis) + S.Score + batch, as.data.frame(colData(from_r)))
python <- read_json("roundtrip/dotted-design.json")
show_table(check = c("terms", "terms equal to Python's", "hash equal to Python's"),
    value = c(paste(colnames(dotted), collapse = ", "), identical(colnames(dotted), as.character(python$terms)), identical(design_sha256(dotted), python$sha256)))
```

## 10. Checking files against the specification

`validate_screen()` and `validate_analysis()` check files against the numbered
rules of `SPEC.md`. They read the files directly, build no `sceptre_object`,
and report every problem they find. The Python library has the same two
functions. What they check about a data file's structure comes from
`spec/screen.json`, about tables from `spec/tables.json`, and about the JSON
records from two JSON Schemas. The example conforms:

```{r}
nrow(validate_screen(screen))
nrow(validate_analysis(file.path(analyses, "left_sided"), screen))
```

`conformance/` holds files that conform and files that each break one rule
(`make_conformance.py` builds them). Three of the broken ones, with what the
validator reports. The first is *readable*: it does not conform, and a reader
must still accept it (S4.4).

```{r}
cases <- jsonlite::fromJSON("conformance/cases.json", simplifyVector = FALSE)
names(cases) <- vapply(cases, function(case) case$name, character(1))
check <- function(case) if (case$kind == "screen") validate_screen(case$path) else validate_analysis(case$path, case$screen)
for (name in c("invalid/screens/counts_as_uint16.h5mu", "invalid/analyses/stage_without_its_predecessor", "invalid/analyses/side_up")) {
    cat(name, ": ", cases[[name]]$what, "\n", sep = "")
    found <- check(cases[[name]])
    print(found, row.names = FALSE, right = FALSE)
    cat("-> ", conformance_level(found), "\n\n", sep = "")
}
```

Every case, with the rules expected and the rules reported:

```{r}
found <- lapply(cases, check)
reported <- lapply(found, function(problems) sort(unique(problems$rule), method = "radix"))
expected <- lapply(cases, function(case) sort(as.character(unlist(case$expect)), method = "radix"))
level <- vapply(found, conformance_level, character(1))
expected_level <- vapply(cases, function(case) case$level, character(1))
show_table(
    case = names(cases), expected = vapply(expected, paste, character(1), collapse = ", "),
    reported = vapply(reported, paste, character(1), collapse = ", "), level = level,
    as_expected = mapply(identical, reported, expected) & level == expected_level
)
```

The four readable files are then read, and give the same counts as the
conforming file each was made from:

```{r}
readable <- names(cases)[expected_level == "readable"]
same_counts <- function(a, b) {
    x <- fmt_read_screen(a)
    y <- fmt_read_screen(b)
    identical(counts(x), counts(y)) && identical(counts(altExp(x, "gRNA")), counts(altExp(y, "gRNA")))
}
show_table(file = readable, reads_to_the_same_counts = vapply(readable, function(name) same_counts(cases[[name]]$path, cases[[name]]$reads_as), logical(1)))
```

```{r}
python <- jsonlite::fromJSON("conformance/results-python.json", simplifyVector = FALSE)[names(cases)]
python_rules <- lapply(python, function(result) sort(as.character(unlist(result$rules)), method = "radix"))
python_level <- vapply(python, function(result) result$level, character(1))
by_level <- function(which) paste(sum(mapply(identical, reported[which], expected[which]) & level[which] == expected_level[which]), "of", sum(which))
show_table(check = c("cases", "conforming files, accepted", "readable files, reported as readable with the expected rules",
    "unreadable files, reported with exactly the expected rules", "rules exercised by a broken file",
    "the Python validator reports the same rules and levels for every case"),
    value = c(length(cases), by_level(expected_level == "conforming"), by_level(expected_level == "readable"),
        by_level(expected_level == "not readable"), length(unique(unlist(expected))),
        identical(unname(reported), unname(python_rules)) && identical(unname(level), unname(python_level))))
```
